newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Sverdlovsk plans 3-mth, $20 mln Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Sverdlovsk plans 3-mth, $20 mln Eurobond.

text.p: Russia's Sverdlovsk region plans to issue a three-month Eurobond for up to $20 million in March 1997, a regional government order obtained by Reuters on Tuesday said.
The plan requires approval by several federal agencies, including the central bank, and the government of Sverdlovsk region, or oblast, which is due to review a detailed plan on December 12.
Sverdlovsk is situated around the Urals city of Yekaterinburg.
Russia's Inkombank has prepared the plan for the region and will sign a contract as financial consultant on the issue after approval by the Sverdlovsk government, the plan said.
The order, dated November 27, said a Western investment bank to lead manage the offering would be chosen by January 30, 1997.
Further issues could be made, based on investor reaction, the government said.
A time-table in the order named September 1997 as the maturity date for a possible six-month issue.
It also said Sverdlovsk would offer collateral, which could be transported outside Russia if necessary, to back the bond.
Proceeds from the bond would be used to fund the regional budget and other programmes.
Sverdlovsk is one of a number of regions and municipalities which intend to issue Eurobonds following the federal government's successful $1 billion issue last month.
The cities of Moscow, and St Petersburg and the Nizhny Novgorod region are all working on such issues.
